parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Surrey · Whalley and City Centre

blocks.text: Living in Bear Creek Green Timbers

parts.t: Bear Creek Green Timbers is an MLS® area in Surrey named for Bear Creek Park and Green Timbers Urban Forest. On the MLS® map it runs roughly from 96 Avenue in the north, with an east edge at about 148 Street south of about 92 Avenue, and reaches at least 84 Avenue in the south. The south and west edges are not confirmed, and all the edges are approximate. Part of Green Timbers Urban Forest may fall in the neighbouring Whalley area.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 13, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Surrey and Surrey Schools.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Homes for sale in Bear Creek Green Timbers
Homes for Sale in Bear Creek Green Timbers Surrey

parts.t: Bear Creek Green Timbers is a well-established Surrey neighbourhood known for its central location, large lots, and easy access to parks, schools, and shopping. The area offers a mix of detached homes, townhomes, and investment opportunities, making it popular with families, investors, and long-term homeowners.

Located near King George Boulevard and Fraser Highway, residents enjoy quick access to transit, major routes, and everyday amenities. The nearby Bear Creek Park and Green Timbers Urban Forest provide walking trails, sports fields, and natural green space that make this one of Surrey’s most balanced communities.
Homes in Bear Creek Green Timbers range from affordable starter properties to larger family homes on spacious lots, offering strong long-term value in a central Surrey location.

blocks.text: Planning in Bear Creek Green Timbers

parts.t: Zoning and plan designations can be different for each lot.
The City’s Fleetwood Plan starts at Green Timbers Urban Forest and runs east along Fraser Highway. Ask the City which plan, if any, covers a specific address.
In 1988 and 1996, Surrey residents voted to designate parts of Green Timbers as urban forest.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Bear Creek Green Timbers

parts.t: Ask the City what is proposed for the lots around the home, especially near Fraser Highway.
Near Bear Creek, check the land.
Ask the City about streamside setbacks and any covenants on title.
Use the Surrey Schools School Locator for the exact address.
For a strata home, read the documents:
the depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees, plus any special levies.
Ask whether it was built with a permit before you count on it.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring.
